examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Scalar Triple Product Using a Determinant
examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $\mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $\mathbf{a},$ $\mathbf{b},$ and $\mathbf{c}.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (2\cdot 2-1\cdot (-1))-2\cdot (0\cdot 2-1\cdot (-1))+(-1)\cdot (0\cdot (-1)-2\cdot (-1)) \\  & =20-2-2 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}b\times c & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot (-2))i-((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot (-2))j+((-1)\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 0)k \\  & =-4i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-4,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the scalar triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =⟨1,2,3⟩\cdot ⟨-4,1,2⟩ \\  & =1\cdot (-4)+2\cdot 1+3\cdot 2 \\  & =-4+2+6 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$
